newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil eyes new peak-hour power rate hike - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil eyes new peak-hour power rate hike - paper.

text.p: The Brazilian government is considering a new hike in electrical rates for the peak consumption hour of 6 p.m. to 7 p.m. in Brazil's industrial heartland to head off possible rationing, local newspapers said.

The papers, quoting federal power holding Eletrobras's President Firmino Sampaio Neto, said the move would aim to slow the growth in power consumption in Brazil's south, southeastern and central-western regions.
Heavy demand for electricity prompted blackouts last Thursday and Friday in Sao Paulo and other southern and southeastern cities.
Eletrobras on Friday called on residential users to refrain from taking showers or using appliances between 6 p.m. and 7 p.m. to avoid excessive demand on the country's power grid.
Folha de S. Paulo newspaper said the Piratininga and Igarape power generators, which had been shut down for maintenance, were restarted to reduce the risk of further blackouts.
